subject: Post-call: Redwood integration & structured output reliability
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration & structured output reliability

Alex — great to meet today, thanks for walking us through the ACME ingestion flow. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we stay aligned:

Summary of call:
- Use case: customer support analytics + assisted-response builder using ACME docs + recent tickets.
- Desired features: structured JSON outputs from the model (structured actions + metadata), embeddings for semantic search, and a lightweight reranker for top-k relevance.
- Constraints: low-latency snippet generation (<= 250ms p50), strict schema validation for downstream parsing, and SSO-based auth for production.

Immediate next steps (what we promised):
1) Send a sample JSON schema and best-practice guide for constrained decoding + validation (attached: structured-output-guidelines.pdf).
2) Share a short SDK snippet showing auth + routing config for Dedicated/Hosted fallbacks.
3) Provide diagram of recommended runtime architecture (attached: redwood-integration-diagram.png).
4) Schedule a 30m technical follow-up with your infra/ML engineering leads to walk through embedding/reranker integration.

Questions for you (to prepare the deep-dive):
- Who will be the primary tech contact(s) from ACME? (include emails)
- Do you need us to support an on-prem Private deployment or will Hosted/Dedicated be sufficient for initial rollout?
- Any compliance constraints (data residency/SOC2 controls) beyond what we reviewed?

Summary of our recommendations (high level):
- Structured output reliability: validate outputs server-side against JSON Schema, implement a 2-step retry pattern (1: constrained decode with temperature=0 + beam/label constraints; 2: if validation fails, a single regeneration attempt with additional context + quality signals).
- Embeddings: use Redwood embeddings for document store; run a lightweight train/threshold for reranker scoring using feature-weighted combination of model logits + semantic similarity.
- Auth/routing: short-lived service tokens for production services + optional per-route cost-based routing (low-latency model variants for snippet generation).

I've attached the artifacts and put a HubSpot note under the deal. Let me know if 10am PT Friday (Mar 6) works for a follow-up with your engineering team.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 08:25:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration & structured output reliability (internal notes)

Internal notes / proposed architecture and code pointers to bring to the call:

Auth & SDK:
- Recommend scoped service account keys + short-lived tokens (15m) for server-to-server calls. For browser-based clients, use Redwood token exchange via your auth provider (OIDC) + minimal claim scope.
- SDK snippet:
  - Initialize client with host override (for Dedicated)
  - Set route policy header (x-redwood-route: low-latency/standard) to pick model variant

Routing & fallback:
- Primary: low-latency model (quantized) for snippet generation.
- Fallback: standard model or different region if latency spike or capacity issue.
- Per-request routing policy via metadata header for cost/perf tradeoffs.

Structured output reliability pattern:
1) Prompt engineering: include system-level instructions + explicit JSON Schema in the prompt. Use delimiter blocks to isolate the schema and the expected output block.
2) Constrained decoding: enable token-level allowlist for structural tokens when possible (e.g., ensure braces/brackets). If model/decoder supports, enable grammar/symbol constraints.
3) Server-side validation: run JSON Schema validation on the generated output. If validation fails:
   - Attempt one synchronous regeneration with tightened constraints (temperature=0, max_tokens same) and include last invalid response as context + explicit correction instructions.
   - If still invalid: return a structured "fallback" payload with an error code and a best-effort parse, log the failure, and surface to calling application to handle.
4) Observability: log validation errors, token counts, latency, model variant, and whether fallback was used. Surface a rate of "schema failures" as a metric for QA reviews.

Embeddings & reranker:
- Compute embeddings for doc corpus (batch offline).
- For query time: retrieve top-N (e.g., 50) via vector similarity, then run a lightweight reranker stage. Two options:
  1) In-server reranker: pass top-N snippets + query to a small reranker model (cheap) and request scores — adds latency but higher precision.
  2) Hybrid score: combine semantic sim score with simple feature-based heuristics (recency, doc_quality) to avoid an extra model call for low-latency paths.

I'll bring a short sample SDK snippet and the JSON Schema template to the Friday call.

-Priyom
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration & structured output reliability

Alex — answers inline to your questions and a few extra details: 

1) Constrained decode details:
- For models that support token/grammar constraints we recommend enabling a small allowlist around structural tokens (commas, brackets, braces, quotes) and required property names. If that's not available, the prompt should include an explicit JSON Schema block and an instruction: "Return only JSON matching the schema between <json>...</json>."
- For long context cases, include a small context window with only the most relevant document snippets + the schema. Large context increases risk of stray text outside the JSON block.

2) Retry logic:
- Recommended: single synchronous regeneration attempt. Empirically, one regeneration with temperature=0 and the invalid output included in the prompt fixes ~70-85% of common schema errors while keeping tail latency acceptable.
- If your app needs higher correctness guarantees, add an async background correction job that can attempt more thorough fixes (multiple regens, structural parsers) and update the content later.

3) Reranker options:
- You can do an in-call reranker with a small dedicated model for top-decisions; Redwood supports a two-stage flow natively (retrieve -> rerank -> generate). If latency is a strict constraint for interactions like UI snippets, hybrid scoring often hits the sweet spot.

Attachments: I've attached the structured JSON schema template and a short checklist for validation+retry patterns (structured-output-guidelines.pdf). Also included the infra diagram for an example Dedicated setup.

I'll send a calendar invite for Fri 10am PT with Priyom and David on the call. For the sandbox key — we can provide a limited-use token scoped to your test environment; please confirm the test hostnames and whether you want embeddings enabled in that sandbox.

Best,
Marissa
